scorecards.inningsCommentary: England embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 521 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 106 from Jos Buttler, complemented by a commanding 169-run stand between Jos Buttler and Ben Stokes that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.0 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by Jasprit Bumrah (5/83), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 317/10 (104.5 ov), England succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as India's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchStory: India posted 329 in the opening innings with Virat Kohli (97) providing key resistance. HH Pandya's 5-wicket haul dismantled England for 161, handing the advantage to India. A ruthless second-innings declaration at 352/7d by India established a massive 521 Runs target. Jasprit Bumrah spearheaded India's attack to bowl out England for 317 and seal victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Trent Bridge commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 329/10 (94.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, England countered with 161/10 (38.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Jos Buttler 106 (176b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Virat Kohli delivered a masterclass for India (200 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 64%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by HH Pandya (70 Runs & 6 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 203 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
